questions.stem: A hospital, school or prison is classified by use as a(n)
questions.explanation: Buildings that house organised public services such as education, health or detention are institutional.

questions.stem: The main purpose of the National Building Code is to
options: fix the selling price of building materials
set minimum standards for the design, construction and safety of buildings
questions.explanation: Building codes and bye-laws set minimum standards for safety, health and planning; prices and company registration are handled elsewhere.

questions.stem: The member of the construction team who prepares the bill of quantities and advises on cost is the
questions.explanation: The quantity surveyor measures and prices the work; the architect designs and the structural engineer designs the structure.

questions.stem: Which item of safety wear protects a bricklayer's head from falling objects on site?
questions.explanation: The hard hat protects the head; boots protect the feet and vests improve visibility.

questions.stem: Wet cement and fresh concrete should not be handled with bare hands for long periods because they
options: are alkaline and can cause skin burns and dermatitis
questions.explanation: Cement is strongly alkaline; prolonged contact burns and irritates skin, so gloves and boots are worn.

questions.stem: The tool used to check that a wall is truly vertical is the
options: plumb bob (or spirit level held vertically)
questions.explanation: A plumb bob hangs vertically under gravity; a spirit level also checks plumb and level.

questions.stem: The machine used to compact hardcore filling under a ground floor slab is the
questions.explanation: Plate compactors consolidate hardcore and soil; mixers only mix concrete.

questions.stem: Removing the vegetable topsoil from a building site before construction is done mainly because topsoil
options: contains organic matter that decays and is compressible
questions.explanation: Organic topsoil shrinks and decomposes, giving settlement; it is stripped and may be reused for landscaping.

questions.stem: The temporary fence erected around a building site to keep out unauthorised persons is the
questions.explanation: Hoarding encloses the site for security and safety; hutments are temporary site huts.

questions.stem: When setting out a right angle by the 3:4:5 method, a builder measures 6 m along one line and 8 m along the other. The diagonal between the two points must be
questions.explanation: 6, 8 and 10 are in the ratio 3:4:5, and 6^2 + 8^2 = 10^2, so the diagonal must be 10 m for a right angle.

questions.stem: Timber boards fixed at the corners of a building outside the trench lines, carrying nails or saw-cuts that mark wall and foundation lines, are
questions.explanation: Profiles hold the setting-out lines in place after excavation removes the pegs.

questions.stem: On a plan drawn to a scale of 1 : 100, a room measures 64 mm long. The actual length of the room is
questions.explanation: Actual = 64 mm x 100 = 6400 mm = 6.4 m.

questions.stem: A drawing showing the external view of one face of a building is called
questions.explanation: Elevations show external faces; plans are horizontal cuts and sections vertical cuts through the building.

questions.stem: A strip foundation trench is 40 m long in total, 600 mm wide and 900 mm deep. The volume of soil to be excavated is
questions.explanation: V = 40 x 0.6 x 0.9 = 21.6 m^3 (before allowing for bulking).

questions.stem: Cutting back the sides of a deep excavation to a safe slope, instead of supporting them with timber, is called
questions.explanation: Battering slopes the sides so they do not collapse; timbering supports vertical sides and dewatering removes ground water.

questions.stem: A foundation consisting of a reinforced concrete slab under the whole building, used on soft soils, is a
questions.explanation: A raft spreads the load over the whole plan area; strip and pad foundations carry walls and columns locally.

questions.stem: Pile foundations are MOST suitable where
options: rock outcrops at the ground surface
the soil is uniform firm gravel near the surface
firm bearing soil lies at a great depth below weak soil
the building is a light single-storey shed on stable ground
questions.explanation: Piles transfer loads through weak upper strata to a firm layer or develop friction along their length.

questions.stem: The damp-proof membrane (DPM) in a solid ground floor is provided to
options: prevent ground moisture rising through the floor slab
questions.explanation: Polythene or similar membranes stop moisture rising; reinforcement and hardcore have other functions.

questions.stem: Which problem is MOST associated with basements in areas of high water table such as parts of Lagos?
options: Water seepage and flooding due to water pressure
questions.explanation: Basements below the water table face hydrostatic pressure and must be tanked or waterproofed.

questions.stem: In a timber upper floor, the members that span between walls and carry the floor boards are the
questions.explanation: Floor joists carry the boarding; purlins and rafters belong to roofs and lintels span openings.

questions.stem: The test carried out on fresh concrete on site to check its workability is the
questions.explanation: The slump cone test measures workability of fresh concrete; cubes test hardened strength.

questions.stem: A 1 : 2 : 4 concrete mix is required for 2 m^3 of concrete. Taking the dry volume as 1.54 times the wet volume, the volume of cement needed is
questions.explanation: Dry volume = 2.0 x 1.54 = 3.08 m^3; cement = 1/7 of this = 0.44 m^3 (about 13 bags at 0.0347 m^3 per 50 kg bag).

questions.stem: Rice husk ash and pulverised fuel ash are used in concrete as
options: pozzolanic materials that partly replace cement
questions.explanation: Pozzolanas react with lime released by cement hydration, allowing part of the cement to be replaced.

questions.stem: Blocks 450 mm long and 225 mm high are laid with 10 mm mortar joints. About how many blocks are needed for 12 m^2 of wall (ignore wastage)?
questions.explanation: Each block with joints covers 0.46 x 0.235 = 0.1081 m^2, i.e. 9.25 blocks per m^2; 12 x 9.25 = 111, say 112 blocks.

questions.stem: A brick bond in which each course consists of alternate headers and stretchers is
questions.explanation: Flemish bond alternates headers and stretchers within each course; English bond alternates whole courses of headers and stretchers.

questions.stem: The common sandcrete block used for external walls of houses in Nigeria measures
questions.explanation: The "9-inch" block is 450 x 225 x 225 mm; 215 x 102.5 x 65 mm is a standard clay brick.

questions.stem: Door frames are secured to block walls during construction with metal
options: holdfasts (cramps) built into the mortar joints
rawl plugs into the frame head
questions.explanation: Holdfasts are screwed to the frame and bedded in the joints as the wall rises.

questions.stem: The horizontal upper surface of a step on which the foot is placed is the
questions.explanation: The tread is the horizontal part; the riser is vertical and the nosing is the projecting front edge of the tread.

questions.stem: A straight flight rises 2.88 m from floor to floor using risers of 160 mm. The number of treads (goings) is
questions.explanation: Risers = 2880 / 160 = 18; a straight flight has one fewer tread than risers because the top floor acts as the last tread: 17.

questions.stem: The water seal in a trap under a sink is provided to
options: prevent foul air from the drain entering the building
measure the flow of waste water
questions.explanation: The trapped water forms a barrier against drain gases while letting waste pass.

questions.stem: The underground chamber that receives sewage from a house and allows solids to settle and decompose before the liquid passes to a soakaway is the
questions.explanation: A septic tank treats sewage by settlement and bacterial action; inspection chambers give access for cleaning drains.

questions.topic: Electrical Installation and Solar Energy System
questions.stem: In a solar energy system, the component that prevents the batteries from being over-charged by the panels is the
questions.explanation: The charge controller regulates panel current into the battery; the inverter converts d.c. to a.c. for appliances.

questions.stem: The timber member fixed on top of a wall to receive and distribute the feet of the rafters is the
questions.explanation: The wall plate spreads rafter loads along the wall; the ridge is at the apex and purlins support rafters mid-span.

questions.stem: A floor finish made of marble chips in cement, ground and polished after hardening, is
questions.explanation: Terrazzo is cast in situ or in tiles, then ground and polished to expose the marble chips.

questions.stem: The cement-sand coat applied to the EXTERNAL face of block walls is called
questions.explanation: Rendering is applied externally and plastering internally; screeds are floor toppings.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common ceiling finishing material in modern Nigerian houses?
questions.explanation: POP and PVC panels are widely used for ceilings; terrazzo and paving stones are floor and external finishes.

questions.stem: Interlocking concrete paving stones on a driveway are laid on
options: a compacted sub-base and a bed of sharp sand
questions.explanation: A well-compacted sub-base with a sand bedding layer supports the pavers; edge restraints hold them in place.

questions.topic: Types of Business Organization and Ways of Raising Capital
questions.stem: A building firm owned by its shareholders whose liability is limited to the amount they invested is a
questions.explanation: Shareholders in a limited company risk only their shares; sole traders and general partners have unlimited liability.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a book of original entry?
questions.explanation: Day books, the cash book and journal are books of original entry; the ledger is posted from them.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT normally a contract document for a building project?
questions.explanation: Contract documents are the agreement, conditions, drawings, specification and bill of quantities; private bank statements are not.

questions.stem:
(a) List the members of the client's team in a building project. [4 marks]
(b) State the functions of (i) the architect (ii) the quantity surveyor (iii) the structural engineer (iv) the site foreman. [8 marks]
(c) Explain the relationship between the client and the contractor. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) Any four, 1 mark each: client; architect; quantity surveyor; structural engineer; services (mechanical/electrical) engineer; project manager; clerk of works
2 marks: (b)(i) Architect: designs the building, prepares drawings and specification, supervises work and issues instructions/certificates
2 marks: (b)(ii) Quantity surveyor: measures and prepares bill of quantities, estimates and controls cost, values work for interim payments
2 marks: (b)(iii) Structural engineer: designs and checks the structural elements (foundations, beams, columns, slabs) for safety
2 marks: (b)(iv) Site foreman: supervises tradesmen on site daily, organises labour and materials and ensures work follows drawings
3 marks: (c) Contractual relationship: the client employs the contractor through a contract (1); contractor builds to drawings/specification for an agreed price and time (1); client pays as certified by consultants (1)
questions.explanation: The client's team is the client and consultants: architect, quantity surveyor, engineers, project manager, clerk of works. The architect designs and supervises; the QS handles cost; the structural engineer designs the structure; the foreman supervises daily work. The client and contractor are linked by a contract: the contractor builds as specified and the client pays on certification.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the procedure for setting out a rectangular building using the 3:4:5 method. [8 marks]
(b) List five tools and equipment used for setting out. [5 marks]
(c) How can the setting out of a rectangle be checked? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
8 marks: (a) 1 mark each step: establish the building line from the site plan; fix pegs A and B on the frontage line at the building length; at A measure 3 units along AB and mark; from A measure 4 units roughly at right angles; adjust so the diagonal between the marks is 5 units, giving a right angle; extend the line to the building width and peg D; repeat at B to fix C; erect profile boards outside the corners and transfer the lines with nails/lines
5 marks: (b) Any five, 1 mark each: measuring tape; pegs; ranging rods; builders' line; builders' square; spirit level; hammer; profile boards; theodolite/level; plumb bob
2 marks: (c) Measure the two diagonals - they must be equal for a true rectangle (also check opposite sides are equal)
questions.explanation: Fix the building line and front corners, use 3-4-5 triangles at each front corner to obtain right angles, measure the width to fix the rear corners, and transfer lines to profile boards. Tools: tape, pegs, ranging rods, line, builders' square, level. Check by equal diagonals.

questions.stem:
(a) Define a foundation and state two of its functions. [4 marks]
(b) Name four types of foundation and state a situation where each is suitable. [8 marks]
(c) State three factors that determine the choice of foundation. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The lowest part of a building which transmits the loads of the structure safely to the ground (subsoil)
2 marks: (a) Any two, 1 mark each: distribute loads over a sufficient area of soil; prevent excessive/uneven settlement; provide a level base for walls; resist movement of the soil
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each (name + situation): strip - load-bearing walls on firm uniform soil; pad - isolated columns of framed buildings; raft - soft or variable soil, heavy loads spread over whole area; pile - firm stratum deep below weak soil; stepped strip - sloping site
3 marks: (c) Any three, 1 mark each: nature and bearing capacity of the soil; type and magnitude of loads; type of building/structure; depth of firm stratum; ground water level; cost; nearby buildings
questions.explanation: A foundation transfers building loads to the soil, spreading them to avoid excessive settlement. Strip (walls on firm soil), pad (columns), raft (soft soil), pile (deep firm layer), stepped (slopes). Choice depends on soil, loads, building type, water table and cost.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between load-bearing and non-load-bearing walls. [4 marks]
(b) A single-room building measures 10 m by 8 m on the centre lines of its walls, and the walls are 3.0 m high. It has one door 0.9 m x 2.1 m and four windows each 1.2 m x 1.2 m. Using blocks 450 mm x 225 mm on face with 10 mm joints, calculate (i) the net area of walling (ii) the number of blocks required, adding 5% for waste. [8 marks]
(c) State three properties of good sandcrete blocks. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Load-bearing wall: carries loads from roof/floors above in addition to its own weight and transfers them to the foundation
2 marks: (a) Non-load-bearing wall: carries only its own weight; used as partition or infill
2 marks: (b)(i) Gross area = perimeter 36 m x 3.0 m = 108 m^2
2 marks: (b)(i) Openings = 1.89 + 5.76 = 7.65 m^2; net area = 100.35 m^2
2 marks: (b)(ii) Blocks per m^2 = 1/(0.46 x 0.235) = 9.25; blocks = 100.35 x 9.25 = 928
2 marks: (b)(ii) Add 5%: 928 x 1.05 = 974.7, say 975 blocks
3 marks: (c) Any three, 1 mark each: adequate compressive strength; uniform size and shape with true arrises; durable/weather resistant; low water absorption; well cured; fire resistant
questions.explanation: Load-bearing walls carry imposed loads; non-load-bearing walls carry only themselves. Gross 36 x 3 = 108 m^2, less openings 7.65 m^2 = 100.35 m^2; 9.25 blocks/m^2 gives 928 blocks, plus 5% = 975. Good blocks are strong, true to size, durable, well cured and of low absorption.

questions.stem:
(a) Define the following drainage terms: (i) gradient (fall) (ii) trap (iii) inspection chamber. [6 marks]
(b) State four principles of a good drainage system. [4 marks]
(c) List five sanitary appliances found in a residential building. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Gradient/fall: the slope given to a drain so that sewage flows by gravity at a self-cleansing velocity
2 marks: (a)(ii) Trap: a bend that retains water (water seal) to prevent foul air from the drain entering the building
2 marks: (a)(iii) Inspection chamber: an access chamber at junctions and changes of direction/gradient for inspecting and rodding drains
4 marks: (b) Any four, 1 mark each: drains laid in straight lines between access points; adequate self-cleansing gradient; watertight joints; adequately ventilated; access at changes of direction; drains of adequate size; protected from damage
5 marks: (c) Any five, 1 mark each: water closet (WC); wash hand basin; bath; shower tray; kitchen sink; urinal; bidet
questions.explanation: Gradient is the fall that gives self-cleansing flow; a trap holds a water seal against foul air; an inspection chamber gives access at junctions and bends. Good drainage is straight, self-cleansing, watertight, ventilated and accessible. Appliances: WC, basin, bath, shower, sink, urinal, bidet.

questions.stem:
(a) Define a contract. [2 marks]
(b) Describe three types of building contract. [6 marks]
(c) List four contract documents. [4 marks]
(d) Name three parties to a building contract. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A legally binding agreement between two or more parties, e.g. client and contractor, to carry out work for an agreed consideration
6 marks: (b) Any three, 2 marks each: lump sum - fixed price agreed before work starts based on drawings and specification; measurement (bill of quantities/schedule of rates) - work remeasured and paid at agreed rates; cost reimbursement (cost plus) - contractor paid actual cost plus a fee or percentage; design and build - contractor designs and constructs; labour-only contract
4 marks: (c) Any four, 1 mark each: articles of agreement; conditions of contract; contract drawings; specification; bill of quantities; schedule of rates
3 marks: (d) Any three, 1 mark each: client/employer; main contractor; architect/consultant (contract administrator); sub-contractors; nominated suppliers
questions.explanation: A contract is a legally binding agreement. Types: lump sum, measurement (BOQ), cost reimbursement, design and build. Documents: agreement, conditions, drawings, specification, BOQ. Parties: client, contractor, consultants, sub-contractors.
